To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker needs to control the content of a template. Whether that is the case depends on the type of application using Jinja. Basic Information for CVE-2025-27516 AIGC Shenlong Model CVE Program / CVE List V5 CNNVD (China National Vulnerability Database) Vulnerability Information Jinja sandbox breakout through attr filter selecting format method Vulnerability Overview Jinja is an extensible template engine. Prior to version 3.1.6, there was a flaw in the interaction between its sandbox environment and the |attr filter. This vulnerability allows an attacker who can control template content to execute arbitrary Python code. Affected Versions All versions below 3.1.6 Vulnerability Details In Jinja's sandbox environment, operations on str.format were supposed to be restricted to prevent sandbox escape. However, by using the |attr filter, an attacker can access the original format method of a string, thereby bypassing the sandbox. This enables the execution of arbitrary Python code. Impact This vulnerability affects applications using Jinja that may process untrusted templates. The attacker must be able to control certain parts of the template content to exploit this vulnerability. Solution Starting from version 3.1.6, the issue has been fixed so that the |attr filter no longer bypasses environment attribute lookups. Users are advised to upgrade to the latest version to prevent exploitation. Have questions about the vulnerability? See if Shenlong's analysis helps! However, it's possible to use the |attr filter to get a reference to a string's plain format method, bypassing the sandbox. After the fix, the |attr filter no longer bypasses the environment's attribute lookup. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.1.6.
